alignments.note: Supplied indefinite *A* joins the noun it determines under rule 15.

The Hebrew writes שָׁמַע once, in the second colon; the ASV writes *heareth* in both, the first italicized for the gapped colon. Rule 34 gives both realizations to the one written verb as a discontinuous unit, headed on the first occurrence. Heading on t011, the occurrence standing in the verb's own colon, was the competing reading.
Construct noun keeps only its own word.
Rectum rendered as an English possessive under rules 19 and 29.
No suffix or other possessive morpheme stands on אָב, so the supplied *his* is added under rule 18's closing sentence.
Waw rendered by the adversative connective the ASV wrote (rule 14).
Supplied *a* joins the nominal expression under rule 15.
Margin *Or, correction* read and set aside under rule 38.

review_notes: The gapped first colon is resolved under rule 34's pro-verb sentence rather than as a supplied lexical verb, because the Hebrew writes שָׁמַע within the coordination.
